Multivariate normal family for several continuous responses

Source: R/families.R
mvn.Rd

For continuous responses measured together on each unit, such as the biomass of several species at a site. The data hold one row per response component at each unit. Latent factors shared by a unit's components give their residuals the covariance Z Z' + diag(Psi^2), where Z holds the factor loadings and Psi each component's residual standard deviation (Hui et al. 2015; Niku et al. 2019). Given the factors, each row is normal with mean mu and standard deviation Psi.

Usage

mvn()

Value

A family object to pass to jsdgam() or mvgam().

Details

jsdgam() fits the family, taking the unit and component columns and the number of factors n_lv. residual_cor() summarises the residual correlations and shared_variation() the part the factors share. Psi takes the prior exponential(1), which suits responses near unit scale. prior(..., class = Psi) sets another.

With K components the data separate the factor part from the residual part only when (K - n_lv)^2 >= K + n_lv. Fewer factors or more components meet the bound. jsdgam() warns when it fails.

References

Hui, F. K. C., Taskinen, S., Pledger, S., Foster, S. D. and Warton, D. I. (2015). Model-based approaches to unconstrained ordination. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 6(4):399-411. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12236

Niku, J., Brooks, W., Herliansyah, R., Hui, F. K. C., Taskinen, S. and Warton, D. I. (2019). Efficient estimation of generalized linear latent variable models. PLOS ONE, 14(5):e0216129. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0216129

Heaps, S. E. and Jermyn, I. H. (2024). Structured prior distributions for the covariance matrix in latent factor models. Statistics and Computing, 34:143. doi:10.1007/s11222-024-10454-0

See also

Other observation families: beta_nb(), categ(), com_binomial(), diri(), multi(), mvgam_families, mvt(), nmix(), occ(), tweedie()

Examples

# \dontrun{
# Five species at 80 sites whose residuals share two latent
# factors
simdat <- sim_jsdgam(family = mvn(), n_species = 5L, n_sites = 80L,
                     n_lv = 2L, seed = 1L)

fit <- jsdgam(
  formula        = y ~ env * series,
  factor_formula = ~ -1,
  data           = simdat$data_train,
  unit           = time, species = series,
  family         = mvn(),
  n_lv           = 2L,
  chains         = 2L,
  silent         = 2
)
#> Warning: 143 of 2000 (7.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
#> Warning: 2 of 2 chains had an E-BFMI less than 0.3.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
summary(fit)
